title: Use an NSString
summary: Objective-C: Use an NSString. Use another name.
introduction: NSString is an object holding text. The @ before the quotes makes an Objective-C string object.

blocks.text: On a Mac with Xcode command-line tools, save lesson.m. Run clang -fobjc-arc -framework Foundation lesson.m -o lesson, then ./lesson.

blocks.title: Use an NSString

blocks.text: The @ literal makes an NSString. UTF8String gives printf a C string.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Plain "Asha" is C text, not an NSString object.
